diagram.documentation:
Definition of the tagged values for stereotype of «mvfElement» used in the MVF profile with mappings to corresponding metamodel attributes

The types assigned to tagged value definitions on this diagram are UML primitives from CCM's standard UML profile, as used by the corresponding MVF XMI attribute, unless changes are indicated by a pale blue note. Note that there is not a one to one correspondence between the attributes of the MVF XMI and MVF RDF classes (see MVF Metamodel - RDF to XMI/PDF equivalent class mappings). Note that these primitives are used in preference to RDF based primitives (e.g. rdf:langString, cmns-txt:Text, which are based on xsd:String; see RDF 1.1 Recommendation, Section 5, Datatypes). This choice is guided by the decision to take the MVF XMI as the primary basis for this metamodel and helps to ensure the portability of the UML profile when deployed in environments without access to this metamodel. When generating RDF based ontologies from UML models built with this profile, consideration should be give to the choice of primitive that these attributes are mapped to - the equivalent RDF properties are asserted indirectly via subsetting relations to attributes of classes in the MVF XMI metamodel, which in turn can be traced via further subsetting relations in the RDF metamodel. Due to the way that CCM imports OWL, OWL properties that are converted to attributes are untyped. Reference to the relevant RDF specification may be required to establish the correct base type. If in doubt, default to typing RDF conversions with RDF 1.1 Datatypes, but note this may result in information loss. The choice of RDF base type is non-trivial as certain choices may not be supported by all tools (see: annotation to cmns-dsg:Designation, annotation to cmns-txt:Text).

 

The tagged value to attribute mappings are split across several diagrams to improve readability. See also MVF Base Profile - Tagged values mapped to metamodel attributes (vocabularyEntry) and MVF Base Profile - Tagged values mapped to metamodel attributes (not mvfElement, vocabularyEntry)

See MVF Base Profile - Class stereotype hierarchy mapped to metamodel types (full) for the inheritance structure of metaclasses and stereotypes.
